scope_split.note: `retry` and the four lifecycle commands share `memory:manage`; `reflect` has its own scope so it can be withheld independently of lifecycle management.

response_shape_note: A lifecycle command has two shapes: a fresh transition returns `before`/`after` and a replay does not. A client that assumes one will break on the other.

recorded.statement: `request_retry` and the lifecycle commands refuse any actor that is not human or system with `ForbiddenActorKind`; `reflect` requires `memory:reflect`, which key issuance will not grant to an agent. Sources: memory/jobs.py, memory/lifecycle.py, memory/api.py.

`reflect` is the only path to the engine's generator and requires an explicit user request; the adapter refuses when `explicit_user_request` is false. A complicated ordinary question goes to recall. It is unreachable from a Context build. Sources: memory/adapter.py, memory/api.py.

A lifecycle command without `expected_revision` is refused with `MissingExpectedRevision`, and a stale one with `RevisionConflict`; the state is checked before the revision so that 'you cannot obsolete a tombstone' is answered as such, and an illegal command appends no Event at all. Source: memory/lifecycle.py.

A retry may not change the job's `document_id`, `content_sha256` or `bank_id`, and a `DONE` job is refused rather than retained twice — a second retain would replace the document. A `RUNNING` job is refused rather than stolen from its worker. Source: memory/jobs.py.
Both the retry and the lifecycle commands are idempotent on `event_id`: a repeat returns the original command Event and writes no second transition. Source: memory/jobs.py, memory/lifecycle.py.
No write here may change Rule or State, and every response that describes memory says it is not Truth. Sources: taskbook §6, memory/api.py.
P4 withholds engine free text from any actor that is not human or system, inside `_respond`, so it applies to every write response too. Source: memory/api.py.

Nothing in this specification is built. There is no b2 route in the dashboard, no b2 path in the proxy allowlist, and no b2 endpoint in the client. Until a permission and audit Gate has run, the write surface must not appear in the product at all.
